profile.name: Rezhky C. W. P. Todingbua, S.Tr.Pel
profile.title: Deck Officer Class II (ANT-II) / Second Officer
profile.subtitle: Maritime Navigation, Bridge Watchkeeping & Vessel Operations
profile.summary: Highly dedicated and disciplined Deck Officer holding Indonesian Deck Officer Class II (ANT-II / STCW II/2) qualification with 1,740+ days (~4.8 years) of verified sea service across General Cargo vessels, Bulk Carriers, and Container ships. Possesses extensive sea-going experience in international and domestic waters, specializing in bridge navigational watchkeeping, passage planning, ECDIS/RADAR navigation, safety compliance (SOLAS/MARPOL/STCW), and vessel deck operations. Committed to the highest standards of navigational safety, situational awareness, and operational excellence.

responsibilities: Carried out bridge navigational watch (12-4 watch: 00:00-04:00 & 12:00-16:00) during international and coastal voyages.
Acted as primary Navigating Officer: formulated comprehensive passage plans, calculated courses, and managed ECDIS electronic charts.
Executed weekly and monthly Notices to Mariners (NtM) chart and publication corrections.
Monitored GMDSS radio equipment, navigational aids, and logged weather reports.
Supervised cargo watch and deck mooring operations in port.
Stood navigational watch on feeder container liner routes with intensive coastal traffic and strait passages.
Conducted berth-to-berth passage planning taking into account squat, under-keel clearance (UKC), tidal windows, and traffic separation schemes (TSS).
Inspected bridge and deck safety gear, distress flares, and portable radio equipment.
Coordinated with port authorities, pilotage services, and cargo surveyors during port turnarounds.
Safely executed navigational watchkeeping under various weather conditions and reduced visibility.
Maintained paper and digital chart inventory, nautical almanacs, and tide tables.
Assisted Master in preparing departure clearances, crew lists, and bridge logs.
Monitored cargo hold ventilation, bilge sounding, and deck security while at anchor and underway.
Performed navigational watch (08:00-12:00 & 20:00-24:00) adhering strictly to COLREG standards.
Assigned as Ship Safety Officer assistant: inspected lifesaving appliances (LSA) and firefighting appliances (FFA) regularly.
Checked lifeboats, life rafts, pyrotechnics, portable fire extinguishers, and SCBA breathing apparatus.
Managed port arrival/departure documentation and cargo lashings verification.
Served as Third Officer on a 27,986 GRT bulk carrier engaged in international dry bulk trades.
Maintained bridge watchkeeping, lookout vigilance, and collision avoidance in heavy traffic waterways.
Maintained vessel muster lists, emergency station bills, and recorded fire/boat drills in official logbooks.
Assisted Chief Officer during dry bulk loading and de-ballasting operations.
Completed one full year of sea phase training for PIP Makassar Training Record Book (TRB).
Trained in bridge watchkeeping, celestial navigation, terrestrial fixes, and radar plotting under officer guidance.
Learned deck maintenance, mooring operations, cargo hold preparation, and painting routines.
Participated actively in shipboard emergency drills and safety meetings.

highlights: Awarded Deck Officer Class III (ANT-III) Certificate of Competency upon graduation, later upgraded to Class II (ANT-II).
Completed comprehensive STCW-compliant officer training in electronic navigation, passage planning, ship handling, stability, meteorology, and maritime law.
Completed 12 months cadetship aboard ocean-going commercial general cargo vessel (MV. BAO LUCKY).
Focus on advanced mathematics, physics, and chemistry.
Active in student leadership and disciplined extracurricular activities.
Core academic foundation and youth leadership development.
Primary education completed in Timika, Papua.
